hand.title: Daily Hand

events.text: Your cards — 5, J. Both players called a raise before the cards were dealt.
Flop — King, 6, Ace. You bet. Your opponent raised.
Turn — 7. Your opponent led out with a bet. You called.
River — 5. Your opponent fired again — half the pot.

wrongReasons: 8 9 is close, but the river lead is the tell. The correct hand picked up more on the river than 8 9 would have.
9 2 makes a flush here — a hand that strong would have raised earlier and pushed harder for maximum value. The measured sizing in this hand points to something weaker.
3 2 has little reason to lead the river here — high card can't comfortably go for value after calling two streets.
hand.explanation:
Answer: 4 3

Your opponent flopped a straight and immediately raised to build the pot. They led every remaining street — consistent value betting across all streets is a strong signal of a made hand.
